answer.answer: You said you could accept losing up to 25%, which is $37,500. So every strategy keeps at least 38.46% in defensive assets, and with your 10-year horizon no more than 61.54% can go into growth assets. The 'core' strategy uses the most growth your limits allow (60%): its worst drop in the past was -13.9%, it returned -9.35% in 2022, and the risk-only view gives a 13.5% chance of ending with less than you put in. 'Income' (50% growth) and 'core-3' (40% growth) were calmer: their worst drops were -9.56% and -11.57%, and each had about a 5.45% chance of ending below what you invested. The 'income' strategy carries one warning: Canada makes up 78% of its stocks, above the 70% guideline, but it passes all the other checks, including your no-fossil-fuel exclusion. These figures describe the past, not a forecast, and the choice is yours.
